mathematicalNotes: Q7: Outer set A = {a, {a, b}} has two elements: a and the inner set {a, b}; its 2² = 4 subsets are ∅, {a}, {{a, b}}, and {a, {a, b}}.
Q8(i): For A = {a, b}, n(A) = 2 gives 2² = 4 subsets in P(A) = {∅, {a}, {b}, {a, b}}.
Q8(ii): For B = {1, 2, 3}, n(B) = 3 gives 1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 8 subsets in P(B).
Q8(iii): For D = {p, q, r, s}, n(D) = 4 gives 1 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 1 = 16 subsets in P(D), formatted across aligned rows for 320px mobile screens.
Q8(iv): For E = ∅, n(E) = 0 gives 2⁰ = 1 subset, so P(E) = {∅} (a one-element set whose sole member is ∅).
Q9(i): W = {red, blue, yellow} has n(W) = 3, giving 2³ = 8 subsets and 2³ − 1 = 7 proper subsets.
Q9(ii): X = {x² : x ∈ N, x² ≤ 100} = {1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100} has n(X) = 10, giving 2¹⁰ = 1024 subsets and 1024 − 1 = 1023 proper subsets.
Q10(i–iii): Apply n[P(A)] = 2^{n(A)} to get 2⁴ = 16, 2⁰ = 1, and 2^{n(A)} = 256 = 2⁸ ⇒ n(A) = 8.
